item.title: Seeking new ways forward
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Seeking new ways forward Canada and EU edge closer as relations with US deteriorate over tariffs Ever since European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen suggested on Sept 16 that Canada considers becoming an "associate member" of the European Union, the two sides have worked rapidly to explore the possibility. Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney welcomed the idea the following day, with both sides seemingly pushed together by the fact that they must diversify their partnerships because they can no longer fully rely on their traditional ally, the United States. On Oct 1, Canada and the European Commission held a new round of Digital Dialogue, with discussions including AI safety, regulation, and innovation. Meeting on the sidelines of the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, US from Sept 30 to Oct 1, Canada's Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu and EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic discussed deepening economic cooperation, with Sidhu highlighting critical minerals, defense, and digital trade as areas where Canada wants more collaboration with the EU. The two sides have already built close economic ties through the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, or CETA, which has been provisionally applied since 2017. Bilateral trade in goods and services reached 130 billion euros ($145.5 billion) in 2025, up 80 percent from 2016. A draft joint statement for the upcoming Canada-EU summit published by The Globe and Mail said the two sides planned to connect next-generation payment systems to enable faster, lower-cost cross-border transactions, while deepening cooperation in areas including critical minerals, digital trade, defense, and space. It added that the new partnership will be called an "Alliance for the Future". The developments echo von der Leyen's words in her State of the Union address, when she said: "We share one ocean, one set of values, one way of seeing the world." Carney struck a similar note in his address to the European Parliament the following day, saying: "An alliance for the future is a unique, positive approach that we will define together, building on our common strengths and based on shared values." The idea builds on years of deepening ties under CETA and gained momentum after the two sides established a Security and Defense Partnership in 2025. Achim Wambach, president of the ZEW-Leibniz Center for European Economic Research, said the alliance could become a blueprint for deep partnerships to secure vital resources and technologies. The Future of European Competitiveness report said that 70 percent of the European cloud and AI market is dominated by US hyperscalers. "The proposed closer partnership with Canada reflects the EU's broader 'de-risking' strategy to strengthen its strategic autonomy by reducing critical dependencies," Wambach said. The European Council's official page on EU-US relations notes that in 2025 the EU imported more than 82.9 billion cubic meters of liquefied natural gas from the US, equivalent to 26.4 percent of total EU gas imports and almost 58 percent of its LNG imports. In comparison, Canada provided 5,384 metric tons of natural uranium to EU utilities in 2025, accounting for 36.7 percent of total deliveries and making Canada the bloc's largest single source. Wambach pointed out that the EU's Critical Raw Materials framework, which includes partnerships with 16 countries, opens the door to more diversification. "Going beyond raw materials, the EU has potential to deepen partnerships with the Gulf region for energy and hydrogen, and India, Japan, and South Korea for advanced technologies and manufacturing," he said. Yan Xiaoxiao, an associate researcher at the Institute of International Relations at the Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences, said a key factor pushing both the EU and Canada to diversify their partnerships is unstable policy from the US. "Canada has been hit by tariffs across sectors including steel, aluminum, autos, and a range of manufactured goods, while the EU agreed with Washington in 2025 to a 15 percent tariff ceiling on most of its exports," he said. "To diversify is important, practical, and beneficial for both sides." Huang Jing, a professor on American studies at Shanghai International Studies University, said the EU-Canada move was not the result of a long period of deliberation backed by corresponding policy and institutional preparations, but an improvised response to immediate pressures. "Whether it can develop into a deeper relationship depends not only on the domestic political constraints on both sides, but also on external factors, primarily the US," he said. Fabian Zuleeg, chief executive and chief economist of the Brussels-based European Policy Centre, said the added value of the proposed relationship would have to come from integration, rather than simply more cooperation. "CETA provides a strong trade framework, but an integrated partnership could go much further: closer integration of markets, finance, and supply chains, alongside economic security, defense procurement, technology, and critical raw materials. But deeper integration must come with obligations as well as benefits, including forms of alignment and sovereignty sharing," Zuleeg said. How far will the diversification go? Radhika Desai, a professor of political studies at the University of Manitoba in Canada, questioned how far such diversification can go, pointing both to Canada's heavy economic reliance on the US and to the institutional hurdles involved in closer integration with the EU. "Canada is so reliant on the United States that it's not going to lead to anything dramatically different," she said, adding that any much closer relationship with the EU would ultimately have to accommodate the interests of its 27 member states. She cited CETA as an example, saying 10 years after it was signed, the agreement is yet to secure ratification from 10 EU countries. Ryan Williams, a former member of Canada's House of Commons, said: "Europe already sells considerably more to Canada than Canada sells to Europe. Are we getting a new political relationship while Europe gets greater access to Canadian resources, defense contracts, investment opportunities, and potentially our market? Those aren't arguments against Europe. They're questions that should be answered before we create a category of EU relationship that has never existed before." According to a September report by independent advisory company Oxford Economics, total trade in goods and services between the EU and Canada has nearly doubled in value during the past three decades, partly thanks to CETA. However, that growth has been driven largely by Canadian imports from the EU, which has widened Canada's trade deficit with the bloc. The report also noted Canada's trade with the EU is roughly one-seventh of its trade with the US. Zuleeg said the arrangement could also have relevance beyond Canada, although not as a one-size-fits-all model. "It could provide a framework for deeper integration with like-minded partners such as the UK, Norway, Japan, or South Korea, potentially complemented by a broader Economic Security Alliance. The central challenge is institutional: how to enable meaningful participation without EU membership, while protecting EU decision-making and ensuring that partners remain genuinely like-minded. It should be flexible, differentiated, and capable of dealing with political divergence over time," he said. Desai argued that Canada should look beyond its traditional Western partners if diversification is its objective. "If you really wanted to diversify your trade relations, you would deepen your relations with China," she said. "Because practically everything that the United States has to offer, you can get from China. Practically everything you have been exporting to the United States, you can sell to China." Canada and the EU are expected to take the discussions further when Canada hosts their next summit in Montreal on Oct 29 and 30. Contact the writers at zhangzhouxiang@chinadaily.com.cn.

item.title: Cold dew brings with it the zest of a Fujian fall
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
In Pinghe county, Fujian province, autumn smells like pomelo. The golden fruit fills family courtyards, lines village roads and piles up in baskets, turning the county into a sea of citrus during harvest season. Oct 8 marks Cold Dew, the 17th of China's 24 solar terms. In Fujian, it comes as pomelos enter their peak harvest season, making the juicy fruit one of the defining tastes of autumn. For many people in southern Fujian, however, a pomelo is more than something to eat. It is childhood memories, family kitchens and the feeling of home. "Pomelos are a very typical autumn food in southern Fujian," said Wu Dongjun, chef and owner of the restaurant fu by MANSION XIA in Xiamen. "When autumn comes, it becomes a regular presence on our dining tables and tea tables." The simplest way to enjoy the fruit is to peel it and eat it fresh. Wu said that some locals add a little salt in order to bring out the sweetness and make the pomelo's fragrance more pronounced. The fruit is also often enjoyed with tea, particularly oolong varieties, such as Tieguanyin, the slight bitterness of which is balanced by pomelo's sweet and tangy flavor. Fujian has a long history of pomelo cultivation, while Pinghe's Guanxi honey pomelo has been grown for more than 500 years. The varieties grown in Fujian have also changed over time. Guanxi honey pomelos were once predominantly white-fleshed. In 1998, a natural mutation was discovered in a Pinghe orchard and later developed through grafting into the red-fleshed variety. The three-red pomelo followed, featuring pinkish-yellow skin, red pith and red flesh. When choosing a good pomelo, locals often look at the fruit's "navel", with a slightly sunken one considered a sign of a juicier, sweeter pomelo. Freshly picked pomelos are often left to rest in a process known as ci shui, or "letting the water settle". As the skin softens, the fruit becomes easier to peel and the flavor develops further. For Fujian cooks, the pomelo rarely stops at the flesh. "People in Fujian are very used to eating pomelo directly, but the fruit can actually be used in many ways," Wu said. "The flesh can go into salads, desserts and even savory dishes." The thick white pith beneath the peel can be soaked, blanched and squeezed repeatedly to remove its bitterness before being braised or stir-fried. It absorbs sauces while retaining a subtle pomelo aroma. Pomelo peel can also be made into preserves, turning what might otherwise be discarded into a sweet snack. That whole-fruit approach has also found its way into Fujian's modern kitchens, where chefs are turning a familiar seasonal ingredient into new dishes and desserts. At his restaurant, Wu uses two Fujian varieties — red-fleshed Guanxi honey pomelo and white-fleshed Duwei pomelo from Xianyou — in a dessert called Autumn Pomelo Assorted Fruit Sweet Soup. The dessert combines the two pomelos with autumn pear, pomegranate, tremella fungus and Minnan-style agar jelly. Together, they bring crispness, juiciness and layered sweetness, with the two pomelos adding contrasting flavors. "I want the dessert to taste like Fujian in autumn," Wu said. "The pomelo gives it a freshness and fragrance that other fruits cannot replace."

item.title: Middle East conflict flares on more fronts
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Middle East conflict flares on more fronts US-Iran standoff lingers as violence in Gaza continues on Oct 7 anniversary The Middle East conflict flared on multiple fronts on Wednesday as indirect talks between the United States and Iran remained deadlocked. Meanwhile, Israelis mourned on the anniversary of the Oct 7 attack as Palestinians live in devastated Gaza. Yemen's Houthi militia struck Aden's international airport with ballistic missiles and drones amid intensified combat on Wednesday. The escalation came after Yemeni government forces, with Saudi-led coalition air support, launched a counteroffensive this week to capture the Red Sea coast around the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait shipping route and the city of Mocha. Yemen's Transport Ministry said in a statement on X that two ballistic missiles and several explosive-laden drones targeted the runway and passenger terminal, with one missile striking near the runway only minutes before Yemenia Airways flight 603 from Cairo was due to land. Aden International Airport is the main international gateway for parts of Yemen outside Houthi control. The Houthis offered no immediate response to the attack. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile north of Riyadh. It added that it was tracking the missile's launch site in Houthi-held Sanaa and planned to destroy the platform, though it released no information on casualties or property damage. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a statement the group targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with multiple drones. Saudi authorities have not yet confirmed the airport attack. Yemen's conflict began in late 2014, when the Houthis seized Sanaa and much of the north. The Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 in support of the internationally recognized government, now based in Aden. Seven months into the broader regional conflict, major powers remain locked in stalemate. Qatar, acting as mediator, said the US and Iran continued indirect negotiations to end their conflict, whose fallout has rippled across the wider Middle East. Despite a ceasefire in April, a June memorandum of understanding and talks at the United Nations General Assembly last month, Washington and Tehran remain sharply divided over the strategic Strait of Hormuz. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said earlier that talks with the US were "meaningless" and only preceded renewed military strikes. US Vice-President JD Vance said in an interview published on Wednesday that Iran must meaningfully scale back its uranium enrichment capacity as a precondition for any war-ending agreement. 3 years on In a parallel development, Israel launched new strikes in Gaza on Wednesday as it marked the third anniversary of the 2023 Oct 7 Hamas attacks. Palestinian officials reported two fatalities. In southern Israel, families mourned at intersections, bomb shelters, and the site of a music festival that the militants overran three years ago in the deadliest attack against Israel. For Palestinians, the anniversary brings another day of misery and difficulties after an Israeli retaliatory campaign in Gaza that has killed tens of thousands of people. The 2023 attack killed 1,200 Israelis and ignited a devastating conflict in Gaza. Palestinian health authorities said more than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed as much of the enclave lies in ruins, and its 2 million residents endure catastrophic living conditions. The anniversary came just 20 days ahead of Israel's first election since the attack, a vote that is viewed as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's long tenure in power. Agencies and Xinhua contributed to this story. Contact the writers at cuihaipei@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Solid-state batteries seen charging sector
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Solid-state batteries seen charging sector 2026-30 period called strategic window to consolidate China's competitive edges China is racing to ensure that all-solid-state batteries become the next extension of its battery sector advantages, turning the nation into a leader in the industry, experts said. They made the comments as seven government authorities — including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology — unveiled last week a plan that set 2030 as the target for the initial large-scale deployment of all-solid-state batteries. The strategy also targets batteries for a much wider application than cars, to now include ships, aircraft, intelligent robots, machinery, power grids, industrial parks and data centers. It calls the 2026-30 period a "strategic window" to consolidate China's global competitive advantages in advanced batteries, while acknowledging weaknesses ranging from insufficient original and disruptive innovation to overcapacity, disorderly competition and gaps in standards and intellectual property. Nan Cewen, an academician at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a professor at Tsinghua University, described the plan as a change in the industry's "competitive paradigm". "It marked the first time China had systematically mapped out the development of the emerging battery industry at the level of a national five-year plan. It signaled a shift in competition from expanding production capacity toward broader rivalry over product value, corporate competitiveness and modernization of the industrial chain. The plan also takes a full-chain approach, covering new battery mechanisms, materials, structures and manufacturing processes," Nan said. Industry investment is already running far ahead of commercial deployment. China announced about 60 new solid-state battery projects in 2025, representing 189 gigawatt-hours of planned capacity and around 67.7 billion yuan ($10.1 billion) of investment, said the Gaogong Industrial Research Institute. In the first half alone, more than 40 solid-state battery and related materials projects were announced, with planned investment exceeding 50 billion yuan. All-solid-state batteries replace the flammable liquid electrolyte versions used in conventional lithium-ion cells with solid materials. In theory, it could improve both safety and energy density, allowing an electric vehicle to travel farther with the same battery weight. Chinese battery makers are increasingly clustering around the same commercialization timetable. CATL has said it is targeting small-scale production of all-solid-state batteries around 2027, while cautioning that the technology remains several stages away from full maturity. BYD has pointed to 2027 for initial vehicle demonstrations, followed by broader deployment around 2030. Gotion High-Tech has disclosed all-solid-state cells with energy density of around 400 watt-hours per kilogram and is developing a 2-gigawatt-hour production line, while EVE Energy this year rolled out new solid-state battery cells from its Chengdu base in Sichuan province as part of its engineering validation program. CALB, another major Chinese battery producer, has been developing higher-energy-density solid-state batteries aimed at cars, robots and aircraft, alongside dedicated pilot production capacity. Ouyang Minggao, an academician at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said some test vehicles equipped with all-solid-state batteries could emerge between late 2026 and 2027, but that large-scale production would "most likely still take another three to five years". China is explicitly looking beyond cars. Its battery plan identifies robots, aviation, shipping, and deep-space and deep-sea applications as potential markets for advanced batteries, reflecting expectations that solid-state technology could first gain traction where high energy density is worth paying for. Liu Wenqiang, Party secretary of the China Center for Information Industry Development, said after the plan was released that China's scale advantage did not guarantee long-term leadership. As Chinese battery makers move closer to the technological frontier, there are fewer mature technologies left to improve upon, Liu said, meaning companies will increasingly need to define tech pathways themselves rather than rely on expansion and incremental upgrading. chengyu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Holiday records strong consumption demand
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Holiday records strong consumption demand China's National Day holiday saw strong demand for smart, green and health-related products, while the consumer goods trade-in program generated 33.48 billion yuan ($4.99 billion) in sales during the first six days of the break, the Ministry of Commerce said on Thursday. Data from the ministry showed that sales of embodied AI robots on major platforms surged 130 percent year-on-year from Oct 1 to 6, while smart glasses sales doubled. During the same period, sales of water-saving devices rose 18.1 percent year-on-year, while those of assistive exoskeletons and outdoor sports equipment increased 12.8 percent and 10.4 percent, respectively, the data showed. The trade-in program also supported spending on major consumer goods. According to the ministry, automobile trade-ins totaled 68,000 vehicles, generating 10.92 billion yuan in new car sales during the period. Home appliance trade-ins reached 2.848 million units, generating 12.34 billion yuan in sales, while purchases of digital and smart products totaled 3.052 million units, worth 8.68 billion yuan, ministry figures showed. Meanwhile, sales at 78 pedestrian shopping streets and commercial districts monitored by the ministry rose 4.7 percent year-on-year, while foot traffic increased 2.5 percent, according to its monitoring data. The ministry said the consumer market remained generally stable throughout the seven-day holiday, with ample supplies of daily necessities and stable prices. Its monitoring of 200 large agricultural wholesale markets showed grain and fruit prices were largely unchanged from Sept 30, while egg, vegetable and pork prices edged down.

item.title: Transport services stepped up for holiday return
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Transport services stepped up for holiday return China stepped up transport services on Wednesday as the National Day holiday drew to a close, with the railways expecting 24.15 million passenger trips during the peak of the return rush. China State Railway Group, the national railway operator, planned to operate 2,449 additional passenger trains. The railways carried 21.61 million passenger trips on Tuesday, marking the third consecutive day that daily passenger trips exceeded 20 million. The holiday had already set a record for daily railway passenger trips, with 25.20 million trips recorded on Oct 1, according to the company. The Ministry of Transport estimated 2.14 billion cross-regional trips from Oct 1 to 7, averaging 306 million a day, up 0.7 percent from the daily average during last year's eight-day Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holiday. Wednesday alone was expected to see 293.75 million trips. The railways were expected to handle 152.36 million passenger trips over the seven days, with the daily average up 13.1 percent year-on-year. Railway bureaus across the country have added services and strengthened connections with local transportation networks to facilitate passengers' return journeys. The Chengdu railway bureau scheduled 154 nighttime bullet train services and arranged for Chengdu East Railway Station to remain open overnight. The Shanghai railway bureau planned to run 557 additional trains and couple train sets on 427 services to increase seat capacity. At Guangzhou South Railway Station, seven passages allow passengers to transfer to the metro without undergoing another security check. Railway stations in Shanghai are also coordinating with metro and bus operators to facilitate journeys. On expressways, authorities and power companies have deployed mobile charging facilities at busy service areas and directed drivers to alternative charging sites to ease queues. Despite a 35 percent year-on-year increase in new energy vehicle traffic, the daily number of service areas experiencing exceptionally heavy charging demand fell 17 percent, the ministry said. China's integrated transport network spans more than 6 million kilometers, including more than 50,000 km of high-speed railways, 199,000 km of expressways and 270 commercial airports. The expanding transport network is giving travelers more options for sightseeing and family visits, including trips to destinations associated with China's revolutionary history. A direct high-speed railway service linking Ruijin in Jiangxi province with Yan'an in Shaanxi province via Yudu in Jiangxi began operating on Sept 6. The service connects several destinations popular for "red tourism", or visits to sites associated with China's revolutionary history. According to China Railway Nanchang Group, Yudu station recorded 65,513 passenger departures during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holiday period through Oct 6, up 57.04 percent year-on-year. Ruijin station handled 69,292 departures, up 52.48 percent. Liu Jinsong traveled with his child from Nanchang to Ganzhou and then to Ruijin. They watched the flag-raising ceremony at Nanchang's Bayi Square before exploring the revolutionary heritage of southern Jiangxi. "High-speed trains make traveling with a child so convenient. They save time and effort, and the service is thoughtful and attentive," Liu said. "My child also learned a lot along the way." Zhang Jumei traveled with her two children to visit relatives in Yan'an on the Ruijin-Yan'an service. "The children couldn't get enough of playing with their cousins," she said. The two families agreed to meet again in Ruijin for Spring Festival. Aviation authorities had also anticipated a possible holiday record. At a news conference in late September, the Civil Aviation Administration of China forecast 31.19 million passenger trips from Sept 25 to Oct 7, covering the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holiday. The daily average was forecast at 2.4 million trips, up 3.6 percent year-on-year, with the peak potentially exceeding 2.6 million. The Ministry of Transport estimated that airlines would carry 16.95 million passenger trips from Oct 1 to 7, averaging 2.42 million a day and remaining broadly unchanged year-on-year. Air passenger traffic on Wednesday was expected to reach 2.51 million trips, up 2.4 percent year-on-year. China Eastern Airlines identified Oct 6 and 7 as the main return peak and planned to deploy larger wide-body aircraft on more than 270 flights between Sept 24 and Oct 8. A traveler surnamed Jiang said that flying from Luzhou in Sichuan province to Tianjin previously took 10 hours, including connections or stops. Lucky Air resumed the route linking the two cities for the holiday. "Now it takes three hours," she said. luowangshu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Cold Dew: Autumn deepens in hue
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
Share - WeChat
When Cold Dew descends, autumn deepens in hue. Chill dew thickens and frost greet the view. Plants turn gold, crabs grace the feast. With a cup of warm tea in hand, that’s where life’s rhythms meet. Tang Dynasty (618-907) poet Bai Juyi wrote in By the Pond: “Cool winds rise and curl, with gentle motion; Cold Dew falls, a chill that stirs emotion.Orchids fade, their petals turn to white; Lotus blooms break, yet leaves stay green and bright.”As cold dew falls, keep warmly clad. item.title: Longer holidays fuel tourism, create spending spree
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-07
Longer holidays fuel tourism, create spending spree More flexible vacation plans by people during the just-concluded Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays have fueled tourism consumption, creating a spending spree both domestically and at overseas destinations. This year's National Day holiday lasted seven days, from Thursday to Wednesday, and some people combined it with the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday to extend their break to as long as 13 days, stimulating both domestic and outbound travel. Figures from travel portal Trip.com Group show that demand for long-distance tours surged during the holiday, with more than 10 percent of people who booked domestic itineraries on the platform extending their vacations to eight days. The proportion was less than 6 percent in 2024. While traditionally popular cities including Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou retained their appeal among tourists, county-level and village destinations demonstrated strong competitiveness during the holiday, thanks to their distinctive local customs, traditions and cuisines, according to travel agencies. Yang Yanying and her 5-year-old son visited Huangling, a village in eastern China's Jiangxi province, during the holiday. The village is known for its Hui-style architecture and the local practice of shaiqiu, or drying crops in bamboo baskets on rooftops or window sills. "It's hard to see and experience such down-to-earth village scenery and life in cities, and it's also a good place for my child to learn about crops and experience the atmosphere of the harvest," said Yang, who lives in Beijing. Online travel agency Qunar said that county and village destinations dominated its top 10 hot spots during the holiday, including Gexian and Huangling villages in Jiangxi province, as well as Jiuzhaigou, a nature reserve and national park in Southwest China's Sichuan province. Chinese people's strong appetite for travel and consumption has also extended to overseas destinations, particularly those which are further afield. A report jointly released by Tuniu and China Mobile on Wednesday showed that visits by Chinese travelers to Canada, South Korea and the Netherlands doubled during the National Day holiday, while trips to Turkiye and Morocco registered year-on-year growth of more than 50 percent. Li Xu, a Beijing resident who traveled to South Korea from Friday to Monday, said he saw many Chinese travelers in Seoul, adding that it really was a "golden week" for tourism. Several of his friends extended their holidays and visited Europe during the break, he added. Yang Han, an analyst at Qunar, said that the nation's more flexible arrangements for taking leave allow people to plan their vacations in more varied ways, which may help reduce travel costs, improve travel experiences and stimulate consumption at destinations. chengsi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Changchun begins games countdown
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-07
Changchun begins games countdown The torch, medals, promotional songs and official uniforms for the Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade were unveiled on Wednesday, which marked the 100-day countdown to the games. The games, featuring 97 events of 12 sports, will be held from Jan 15 to 25, 2027, in Changchun and Jilin cities of Jilin province. The name of the torch is "Ji Xiang", with "Ji" standing for Jilin province and also implying good fortune, and "Xiang" meaning to soar, said Guo Chunfang, dean of the Art College of Jilin University and one of the chief designers of the torch. The torch is 711 millimeters in height, referencing Changchun's highest-elevation landmark, which stands at 711 meters above sea level, he said. Its material distinguishes it from previous torches. The upper section is made of alloy, and the lower section uses carbon-fiber material independently developed in Jilin province. This carbon-fiber material is lightweight, safe and resistant to high temperatures, he said. Instead of simply pasting urban cultural symbols onto the surface, the designers have integrated local themes into the torch. Twelve film-themed icons represent the 12 sports of the Changchun games, and pay tribute to Changchun's status as a film city, Guo said. The side profile draws inspiration from a snowboard. On the top, patterns of clivia — Changchun's city flower — and snowflakes are stylized into the image of young people embracing each other, embodying the spirit of the games. At the bottom, an automobile carving celebrates Changchun's reputation as an automotive city, he said. The medal, named "Ji Meng", or "auspicious dreams", continues the "Ji" theme and echoes the games' slogan of "Dreams Ignited, Youth United", according to the organizing committee. The front of the medal is inspired by traces of ice skates and snowboards gliding over ice and snow, while the back features the "first jade bird of ancient China", a Neolithic jade artifact from 7,000 years ago, the committee said. A chip embedded in the medal allows athletes to view images of their medal-ceremony moments and Changchun's scenery across the four seasons with a tap of a smartphone, it said. Two promotional songs and six series of official uniforms for the games were also released. Zhang Enhui, secretary of the Communist Party of China Changchun Municipal Committee, extended a sincere invitation to guests from across the globe. Located at a latitude of 43 degrees north in a golden ice-and-snow belt, Changchun has a snow season lasting up to four months and powdery snow. Having hosted the Asian Winter Games and the National Winter Games, the city has ice and snow in its DNA, with winter sports deeply woven into daily life, he added. Changchun has now entered "Universiade time", Zhang said. From the construction of venues and urban upgrading to service improvements, residents are fully prepared and eager to welcome visitors from around the world, he added.

item.title: Visionary Pathway: The Enduring Voice of Minju Opera
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-07
Visionary Pathway: The Enduring Voice of Minju Opera Share - WeChat
For more than four centuries, Minju Opera has been part of Fuzhou's cultural identity. But in the 1980s, the art form faced a fight for survival. Xi Jinping, who served as Party secretary of Fuzhou from 1990 to 1996, championed a series of measures to preserve it — from securing stable funding for theater troupes to establishing a dedicated training school. Today, thanks to decades of sustained efforts, the ancient art form has found new life and continues to inspire new generations.
